target_claim: For a graph G on n vertices whose maximum independent-set size is k, the strictly upper-triangular part UA of its adjacency matrix satisfies (UA)^(n-k+1)=θ, and conversely.
source_quote:
CLAIM 1 : Given an integer k≤n and a graph G on n vertices, let A denote its 
adjacency matrix, and UA the strictly upper triangular matrix extracted from A. 
Then G  contains a maximum independent set of size k if and only if (UA)n-k+1=θ.
